newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten says need for HK rights curbs still unclear.
newsitem.headline: Patten says need for HK rights curbs still unclear.

text.p: Governor Chris Patten said on Thursday the future Hong Kong government's revised proposals on civil rights curbs still failed to clarify why such a move was necessary.
"I note that the original proposals have, to some extent, been modified in the light of the strong public reaction last month," Patten said in a statement.
"But the central question that people have been asking about this exercise remains unanswered, and that is why any of it should be necessary," he said.

Michael Suen, an aide to future leader Tung Chee-hwa, earlier on Thursday unveiled a diluted version of curbs on demonstrations and a modified ban on foreign funding of local political groups after the British colony reverts to China on July 1.

Suen said changes were made after digesting views canvassed during a three-week public consultation exercise marked by strong opposition from the pro-democracy camp to any rollback of political freedoms and rights.
Patten said the modified proposals were essentially similar to the original ones.

"They still introduce the concept of having to seek permission to demonstrate. They still require societies to apply for registration, and provide for cancellation of registration if a society accepts a financial contribution from a foreign political organisation. And they still confuse public order considerations with the totally separate and nebulous notion of national security," the governor said.
Patten said present laws worked perfectly well and public order in Hong Kong was as good as it was anywhere in the world.
